A per-workspace flock serializes claim operations so\n//! workers take turns rather than racing on the same bead.\n//!\n//! Depends on: `types`, `bead_store`, `telemetry`.\n\nuse std::collections::HashSet;\nuse std::hash::{Hash, Hasher};\nuse std::io;\nuse std::path::{Path, PathBuf};\nuse std::sync::Arc;\nuse std::time::{Duration, Instant};\n\nuse anyhow::{anyhow, Result};\nuse fs2::FileExt;\n\nuse crate::bead_store::BeadStore;\nuse crate::telemetry::{EventKind, Telemetry};\nuse crate::types::{Bead, BeadId, BeadStatus, ClaimOutcome, ClaimResult};\n\n/// Flock timeout: maximum time to wait for the workspace lock.\nconst FLOCK_TIMEOUT: Duration = Duration::from_secs(10);\n\n/// Flock poll interval: time between lock acquisition attempts.\nconst FLOCK_POLL_INTERVAL: Duration = Duration::from_millis(50);\n\n/// Atomic bead claimer with workspace-level flock serialization.\npub struct Claimer {\n    store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,\n    lock_dir: PathBuf,\n    max_retries: u32,\n    retry_backoff_ms: u64,\n    telemetry: Telemetry,\n}\n\nimpl Claimer {\n    /// Create a new Claimer.\n    ///\n    /// - `store`: bead store for verify + claim operations\n    /// - `lock_dir`: directory for flock files (default: `/tmp`)\n    /// - `max_retries`: maximum claim attempts before giving up (default: 5)\n    /// - `retry_backoff_ms`: base backoff between retries in ms (default: 100)\n    /// - `telemetry`: telemetry emitter\n    pub fn new(\n        store: Arc<dyn BeadStore>,\n        lock_dir: PathBuf,\n        max_retries: u32,\n        retry_backoff_ms: u64,\n        telemetry: Telemetry,\n    ) -> Self {\n        Claimer {\n            store,\n            lock_dir,\n            max_retries,\n            retry_backoff_ms,\n            telemetry,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt to claim the next available bead from the candidate list.\n    ///\n    /// Iterates candidates in priority order, skipping those in the exclusion\n    /// set. For each candidate, acquires a per-workspace flock, verifies the\n    /// bead is still claimable, and attempts the claim.\n    ///\n    /// The `strand` parameter is the name of the strand that initiated the claim\n    /// (e.g., \"pluck\", \"mend\"). fn claim_next(\n        &self,\n        candidates: &[Bead],\n        actor: &str,\n        exclusions: &HashSet<BeadId>,\n        strand: &str,\n    ) -> Result<ClaimOutcome> {\n        let eligible: Vec<&Bead> = candidates\n            .iter()\n            .filter(|b| !exclusions.contains(&b.id))\n            .collect();\n\n        if eligible.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(ClaimOutcome::NoCandidates);\n        }\n\n        let mut attempts = 0u32;\n\n        for candidate in &eligible {\n            if attempts >= self.max_retries {\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"max_retries_exceeded\");\n                // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", \"max_retries_exceeded\");\n                return Ok(ClaimOutcome::AllRaceLost);\n            }\n\n            attempts += 1;\n            let bead_id = &candidate.id;\n\n            // Set bead_id and retry_number as span attributes.\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.bead.id\", bead_id.as_ref());\n            tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.retry_number\", attempts);\n\n            self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimAttempt {\n                bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                attempt: attempts,\n            })?;\n\n            // Compute workspace lock path\n            let lock_path = workspace_lock_path(&self.lock_dir, &candidate.workspace);\n\n            // Acquire flock with timeout\n            let lock_file = match acquire_flock(&lock_path).await {\n                Ok(f) => f,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::warn!(bead_id = %bead_id, error = %e, \"flock timeout, skipping\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: format!(\"flock timeout: {e}\"),\n                    })?;\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current()\n                        .record(\"otel.status_description\", format!(\"flock timeout: {e}\"));\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                }\n            };\n\n            // Verify bead is still claimable (status=open, no assignee)\n            let current = match self.store.show(bead_id).await {\n                Ok(b) => b,\n                Err(e) => {\n                    drop(lock_file);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: format!(\"verify failed: {e}\"),\n                    })?;\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current()\n                        .record(\"otel.status_description\", format!(\"verify failed: {e}\"));\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                }\n            };\n\n            if current.status != BeadStatus::Open || current.assignee.is_some() {\n                drop(lock_file);\n                // Distinguish stale-assignee from race-lost: race_lost means another worker\n                // won the race (status changed), not that this bead has a leftover assignee.\n                if current.status == BeadStatus::Open && current.assignee.is_some() {\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: \"stale assignee\".to_string(),\n                    })?;\n                } else {\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                }\n                // Apply backoff before trying next candidate (same as store.claim RaceLost path)\n                if attempts < self.max_retries {\n                    tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(\n                        self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),\n                    ))\n                    .await;\n                }\n                continue;\n            }\n\n            // Attempt claim via store\n            let result = self.store.claim(bead_id, actor).await;\n            drop(lock_file);\n\n            match result {\n                Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead)) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"succeeded\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimSuccess {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        priority: candidate.priority as i32,\n                        strand: strand.to_string(),\n                    })?;\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::Claimed(bead));\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { .. }) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", \"race_lost\");\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimRaceLost {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    if attempts < self.max_retries {\n                        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(\n                            self.retry_backoff_ms * u64::from(attempts),\n                        ))\n                        .await;\n                    }\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason }) => {\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    continue;\n                }\n                Err(e) => {\n                    let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                    self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                        bead_id: bead_id.clone(),\n                        reason: reason.clone(),\n                    })?;\n                    // Set Error status on the bead.claim span\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", reason);\n                    return Ok(ClaimOutcome::StoreError(e));\n                }\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Exhausted all eligible candidates without success\n             bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable { reason })\n            }\n            Ok(other) => {\n                // RaceLost shouldn't happen with claim_auto, but handle it\n                tracing::warn!(?other, \"claim_auto returned unexpected result\");\n                Ok(other)\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                let reason = format!(\"store error: {e}\");\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"needle.claim.result\", &reason);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n                tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_description\", &reason);\n                self.telemetry.emit(EventKind::ClaimFailed {\n                    bead_id: BeadId::from(\"(auto)\".to_string()),\n                    reason: reason.clone(),\n                })?;\n                Err(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Compute a deterministic lock file path for a workspace.\n///\n/// Uses a simple hash (not crypto) of the workspace path. Deserialize)]\n141\t#[serde(rename_all = \"SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE\")]\n142\tpub enum WorkerState {\n143\t    Booting,\n144\t    Selecting,\n145\t    Claiming,\n146\t    Retrying,\n147\t    Building,\n148\t    Dispatching,\n149\t    Executing,\n150\t    Handling,\n151\t    Logging,\n152\t    /// All strands returned empty — worker has nothing to do.\n153\t    Exhausted,\n154\t    /// Received graceful shutdown signal.\n155\t    Stopped,\n156\t    /// Unrecoverable error.\n157\t    Errored,\n158\t}\n159\t\n160\timpl fmt::Display for WorkerState {\n161\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n162\t        let s = match self {\n163\t            WorkerState::Booting => \"BOOTING\",\n164\t            WorkerState::Selecting => \"SELECTING\",\n165\t            WorkerState::Claiming => \"CLAIMING\",\n166\t            WorkerState::Retrying => \"RETRYING\",\n167\t            WorkerState::Building => \"BUILDING\",\n168\t            WorkerState::Dispatching => \"DISPATCHING\",\n169\t            WorkerState::Executing => \"EXECUTING\",\n170\t            WorkerState::Handling => \"HANDLING\",\n171\t            WorkerState::Logging => \"LOGGING\",\n172\t            WorkerState::Exhausted => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n173\t            WorkerState::Stopped => \"STOPPED\",\n174\t            WorkerState::Errored => \"ERRORED\",\n175\t        };\n176\t        f.write_str(s)\n177\t    }\n178\t}\n179\t\n180\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n181\t// Outcome\n182\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n183\t\n184\t/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n185\t///\n186\t/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n187\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\n188\tpub enum Outcome {\n189\t    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n190\t    Success,\n191\t    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n192\t    Failure,\n193\t    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n194\t    Timeout,\n195\t    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n196\t    AgentNotFound,\n197\t    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n198\t    Interrupted,\n199\t    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n200\t    Crash(i32),\n201\t}\n202\t\n203\timpl Outcome {\n204\t    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n205\t    ///\n206\t    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n207\t    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n208\t    ///\n209\t    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n210\t    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n211\t    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n212\t    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n213\t    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n214\t    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n215\t    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n216\t    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n217\t    /// - all other → `Failure`\n218\t    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n219\t        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n220\t        if was_interrupted {\n221\t            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n222\t        }\n223\t\n224\t        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n225\t        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n226\t        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n227\t        match exit_code {\n228\t            // Success\n229\t            0 => Outcome::Success,\n230\t            // Explicit failure code\n231\t            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n232\t            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n233\t            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n234\t            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n235\t            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n236\t            // Failure range: 2-123\n237\t            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n238\t            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n239\t            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n240\t            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n241\t            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n242\t            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n243\t            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n244\t            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n245\t        }\n246\t    }\n247\t\n248\t    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n249\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n250\t        match self {\n251\t            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n252\t            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n253\t            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n254\t            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n255\t            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n256\t            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n257\t        }\n258\t    }\n259\t}\n260\t\n261\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n262\t// StrandError / StrandResult\n263\t// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n264\t\n265\t/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n266\t#[derive(Debug)]\n267\tpub enum StrandError {\n268\t    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n269\t    ConfigError(String),\n270\t}\n271\t\n272\timpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n273\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n274\t        match self {\n275\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n276\t                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n277\t                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n278\t                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n279\t                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n280\t                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n281\t                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n282\t                }\n283\t                Ok(())\n284\t            }\n285\t            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n286\t        }\n287\t    }\n288\t}\n289\t\n290\timpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n291\t    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n292\t        match self {\n293\t            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n294\t            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n295\t        }\n296\t    }\n297\t}\n298\t\n299\t/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n300\t#[non_exhaustive]\n301\t#[derive(Debug)]\n302\tpub enum StrandResult {\n303\t    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n304\t    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n305\t    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n306\t    WorkCreated,\n307\t    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n308\t    NoWork,\n309\t    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n310\t    Error(StrandError),\n311\t    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n312\t    ///\n313\t    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n314\t    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n315\t}\n316\t\n317\t// Lower number = higher priority (P1 > P2 > P3).\npub type Priority = u8;\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BeadStatus\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Lifecycle status of a bead in the store.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum BeadStatus {\n    Open,\n    InProgress,\n    /// `bf` (bead-forge) has been observed emitting `\"completed\"` for done\n    /// beads on some workspaces (bf's own `Status` enum has no `Completed`\n    /// variant — it falls through to an untagged `Custom(String)`, so this\n    /// slips through bf-side validation). Accept it as an alias so a single\n    /// such bead doesn't fail `bf list --json` deserialization for every\n    /// other bead in the same call — see needle-weave-completed-status.\n    #[serde(alias = \"completed\")]\n    Done,\n    /// `br show --json` emits `\"closed\"` for done beads. Treat as equivalent\n    /// to `Done` so deserialization succeeds.\n    Closed,\n    Blocked,\n}\n\nimpl BeadStatus {\n    /// Returns true if the bead is finished (either `Done` or `Closed`).\n    pub fn is_done(&self) -> bool {\n        matches!(self, BeadStatus::Done | BeadStatus::Closed)\n    }\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BeadStatus {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            BeadStatus::Open => write!(f, \"open\"),\n            BeadStatus::InProgress => write!(f, \"in_progress\"),\n            BeadStatus::Done | BeadStatus::Closed => write!(f, \"done\"),\n            BeadStatus::Blocked => write!(f, \"blocked\"),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// WorkerState\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Worker finite-state-machine states.\n///\n/// Every state has defined entry conditions, actions, and exit transitions.\n/// There are no implicit states or fallthrough paths.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE\")]\npub enum WorkerState {\n    Booting,\n    Selecting,\n    Claiming,\n    Retrying,\n    Building,\n    Dispatching,\n    Executing,\n    Handling,\n    Logging,\n    /// All strands returned empty — worker has nothing to do.\n    Exhausted,\n    /// Received graceful shutdown signal.\n    Stopped,\n    /// Unrecoverable error.\n    Errored,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for WorkerState {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        let s = match self {\n            WorkerState::Booting => \"BOOTING\",\n            WorkerState::Selecting => \"SELECTING\",\n            WorkerState::Claiming => \"CLAIMING\",\n            WorkerState::Retrying => \"RETRYING\",\n            WorkerState::Building => \"BUILDING\",\n            WorkerState::Dispatching => \"DISPATCHING\",\n            WorkerState::Executing => \"EXECUTING\",\n            WorkerState::Handling => \"HANDLING\",\n            WorkerState::Logging => \"LOGGING\",\n            WorkerState::Exhausted => \"EXHAUSTED\",\n            WorkerState::Stopped => \"STOPPED\",\n            WorkerState::Errored => \"ERRORED\",\n        };\n        f.write_str(s)\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Outcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// The classified outcome of an agent process.\n///\n/// Every exit code maps to exactly one variant via `Outcome::classify()`.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum Outcome {\n    /// Exit 0 — agent completed work successfully.\n    Success,\n    /// Non-zero exit indicating a failure (includes app errors 1-99 and unknown codes).\n    Failure,\n    /// Exit 100 or 124 — timeout wrapper expired.\n    Timeout,\n    /// Exit 126 or 127 — agent binary not found or not executable.\n    AgentNotFound,\n    /// Exit 130 (SIGINT) or 143 (SIGTERM) — agent was interrupted.\n    Interrupted,\n    /// Negative exit code — process crashed or was killed by a signal.\n    Crash(i32),\n}\n\nimpl Outcome {\n    /// Classify an exit code into an `Outcome` variant.\n    ///\n    /// Every exit code range has an explicit match arm — no wildcards.\n    /// The `was_interrupted` flag takes precedence over exit code analysis.\n    ///\n    /// # Mapping (per spec)\n    /// - `was_interrupted=true` → `Interrupted` (checked first)\n    /// - exit 0 → `Success`\n    /// - exit 1 → `Failure`\n    /// - exit 124 → `Timeout`\n    /// - exit 127 → `AgentNotFound`\n    /// - exit >128 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - exit <0 → `Crash(exit_code)`\n    /// - all other → `Failure`\n    pub fn classify(exit_code: i32, was_interrupted: bool) -> Self {\n        // Interrupted flag takes precedence (graceful shutdown path).\n        if was_interrupted {\n            return Outcome::Interrupted;\n        }\n\n        // Explicit mapping for every exit code range — NO wildcards.\n        // Each range is explicitly enumerated to ensure compile errors\n        // if a new Outcome variant is added without updating this match.\n        match exit_code {\n            // Success\n            0 => Outcome::Success,\n            // Explicit failure code\n            1 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Timeout (GNU timeout exit code)\n            124 => Outcome::Timeout,\n            // Agent not found (shell exit code for missing command)\n            127 => Outcome::AgentNotFound,\n            // Failure range: 2-123\n            2..=123 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Failure: 125-128 (not >128 per spec, so 128 is not Crash)\n            125..=128 => Outcome::Failure,\n            // Signal exits: >128 (128 + signal number)\n            // These are all crashes per the spec.\n            129..=i32::MAX => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n            // Negative exit codes (abnormal termination)\n            i32::MIN..=-1 => Outcome::Crash(exit_code),\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Return a string representation for telemetry/logging.\n    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n        match self {\n            Outcome::Success => \"success\",\n            Outcome::Failure => \"failure\",\n            Outcome::Timeout => \"timeout\",\n            Outcome::AgentNotFound => \"agent_not_found\",\n            Outcome::Interrupted => \"interrupted\",\n            Outcome::Crash(_) => \"crash\",\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// StrandError / StrandResult\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Error returned by a strand evaluation.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandError {\n    StoreError(anyhow::Error),\n    ConfigError(String),\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for StrandError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => {\n                // Show the full error chain, not just the top-level context.\n                // This surfaces the actual stderr/stdout from bf/br commands.\n                write!(f, \"bead store error: {}\", e)?;\n                // Append any error causes from the chain (the actual bf/br stderr)\n                for cause in e.chain().skip(1) {\n                    write!(f, \"\\n  caused by: {}\", cause)?;\n                }\n                Ok(())\n            }\n            StrandError::ConfigError(s) => write!(f, \"strand configuration error: {}\", s),\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for StrandError {\n    fn source(&self) -> Option<&(dyn std::error::Error + 'static)> {\n        match self {\n            StrandError::StoreError(e) => Some(e.as_ref()),\n            StrandError::ConfigError(_) => None,\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n/// Result of a strand evaluation in the waterfall.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum StrandResult {\n    /// One or more candidate beads were found.\n    BeadFound(Vec<Bead>),\n    /// The strand synthesized new work (e.g., mitosis created child beads).\n    WorkCreated,\n    /// This strand found nothing; continue to the next strand.\n    NoWork,\n    /// The strand encountered an error during evaluation.\n    Error(StrandError),\n    /// A bead with too many consecutive failures should be split.\n    ///\n    /// Contains the bead to split and the current failure count.\n    Split(Box<Bead>, u32),\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ClaimResult / ClaimOutcome\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Result of a single claim attempt for one bead.\n#[non_exhaustive]\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum ClaimResult {\n    /// This worker successfully claimed the bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Another worker claimed the bead first.\n    RaceLost {\n        /// Assignee that won the race.\n        claimed_by: String,\n    },\n    /// The bead cannot be claimed (not open, blocked, etc.).\n    NotClaimable {\n        /// Human-readable reason.\n        reason: String,\n    },\n}\n\n/// Aggregate bead.\n    Claimed(Bead),\n    /// Raced every candidate and lost every time.\n    AllRaceLost,\n    /// The strand returned no candidates.\n    NoCandidates,\n    /// The bead store returned an ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// A bead dependency as returned from the `br` JSON output.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]\npub ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// Bead struct\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Serde helper: treats an empty JSON string as `None`.\nfn empty_string_as_none<'de, D>(d: D) -> Result<Option<String>, D::Error>\nwhere\n    D: serde::Deserializer<'de>,\n{\n    let s = ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// NeedleError\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Top-level NEEDLE error type.\n///\n/// Tier is encoded in the variant, so recovery routing is type-driven.\n#[derive(Debug)]\npub enum NeedleError {\n    /// Transient: retry after backoff (network hiccup, lock bead_id: BeadId },\n    /// Worker-scoped: this worker should shut down; fleet continues.\n    WorkerScoped {\n        message: String,\n        worker_id: WorkerId,\n    },\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for NeedleError {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: Some(id),\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error (bead {}): {}\", id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::Transient {\n                message,\n                bead_id: None,\n            } => {\n                write!(f, \"transient error: {}\", message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::BeadScoped { message, bead_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"bead-scoped error (bead {}): {}\", bead_id, message)\n            }\n            NeedleError::WorkerScoped { message, worker_id } => {\n                write!(f, \"worker-scoped error (worker {}): {}\", worker_id, message)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl std::error::Error for NeedleError {}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// What a worker does when the queue is empty.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]\n#[serde(rename_all = \"snake_case\")]\npub enum IdleAction {\n    /// Poll again after `idle_timeout` seconds.\n    #[default]\n    Wait,\n    /// Exit cleanly.\n    Exit,\n}\n\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n// BeadAction\n// ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// Action taken on a bead by the outcome handler.\n#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]\npub enum BeadAction {\n    /// Bead was released back to open status.\n    Released,\n    /// Bead was deferred (e.g., timeout with deferred label).\n    Deferred,\n    /// An alert bead was created.\n    Alerted,\n    /// No action taken (e.g., success with bead already closed).\n    None,\n}\n\nimpl fmt::Display for BeadAction {\n    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n        match self {\n            BeadAction::Released => write!(f, \"released\"),\n            BeadAction::Deferred => Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. Verify: br doctor\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if rebuild or verification fails (JSONL itself may be corrupt).\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()>;\n}\n\n// ─── BrCliBeadStore ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `br` CLI-backed bead store implementation.\n///\n/// All operations shell out to `br` with `--json` output and parse the result.\n/// The workspace directory is set via `BEADS_PATH` / cwd when invoking br.\npub struct BrCliBeadStore {\n    /// Path to the `br` binary.\n    pub br_path: PathBuf,\n    /// Workspace root (directory containing `.beads/`).\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n}\n\nimpl BrCliBeadStore {\n    /// Construct a new store, validating that the `br` binary exists.\n    pub fn new(br_path: PathBuf, workspace: PathBuf) -> Result<Self> {\n        if !br_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\"br binary not found at {}\", br_path.display());\n        }\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore { br_path, workspace })\n    }\n\n    /// Try to find `br` on PATH or the default install location.\n    pub fn discover(workspace: PathBuf) -> Result<Self> {\n        let br_path = which::which(\"br\")\n            .or_else(|_| {\n                let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n                let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/br\"));\n                if candidate.exists() {\n                    Ok(candidate)\n                } else {\n                    Err(anyhow!(\"br not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/br\"))\n                }\n            })\n            .context(\"br CLI not found; install beads_rust\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore { br_path, workspace })\n    }\n\n    /// Default timeout for br subprocess calls (30 seconds).\n    const DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;\n\n    /// Run a `br` subcommand in the workspace directory and return stdout.\n    ///\n    /// Returns `Err` if the process fails to spawn, exits non-zero (unless\n    /// the caller handles specific codes), or stdout is not valid UTF-8.\n    async fn run_br(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_br_in(&self.workspace, args, Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    /// Run a `br` subcommand with a custom timeout.\n    ///\n    /// Use this for calls that may take longer (e.g., sync operations).\n    #[allow(dead_code)]\n    async fn run_br_with_timeout(&self, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_br_in(&self.workspace, args, timeout_secs).await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_br_in(&self, dir: &Path, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);\n\n        // kill_on_drop ensures the process is killed if the wait_with_output\n        // future is dropped (e.g., on timeout), preventing orphaned br processes.\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        // Wait for output with timeout. On timeout, kill_on_drop fires automatically.\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"br subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"br subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\"br subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"br stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).into_owned();\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n\n            // FrankenSQLite crash recovery: if br was killed by a signal\n            // (code() returns None) but stdout shows the operation completed\n            // and stderr is empty, treat as success. This commonly happens\n            // when br's SQLite layer crashes during post-commit cleanup while\n            // the mutation was already persisted to the append-only JSONL file.\n            if output.status.code().is_none() && stderr.is_empty() && !stdout.is_empty() {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    stdout = %stdout.trim(),\n                    \"br was killed by signal but stdout indicates success — \\\n                     treating as successful (FrankenSQLite crash recovery)\"\n                );\n                return Ok(stdout);\n            }\n\n            // Auto-recover from SYNC_CONFLICT: run `br sync` then retry once.\n            if is_sync_conflict(&stderr) {\n                tracing::warn!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    \"br hit SYNC_CONFLICT, running br sync and retrying\"\n                );\n\n                let sync_timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(60);\n                let mut sync_cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n                sync_cmd\n                    .args([\"sync\"])\n                    .current_dir(dir)\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .kill_on_drop(true);\n                let sync_child = sync_cmd\n                    .spawn()\n                    .context(\"failed to spawn br sync during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\")?;\n\n                let sync_output = match tokio::time::timeout(\n                    sync_timeout,\n                    sync_child.wait_with_output(),\n                )\n                .await\n                {\n                    Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n                    Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                        return Err(e).context(\"br sync failed during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\");\n                    }\n                    Err(_) => {\n                        tracing::error!(\"br sync timed out after 60s during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery, killing process\");\n                        bail!(\"br sync timed out after 60s during SYNC_CONFLICT recovery\");\n                    }\n                };\n\n                if !sync_output.status.success() {\n                    let sync_stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&sync_output.stderr);\n                    tracing::warn!(stderr = %sync_stderr, \"br sync failed, retrying original command anyway\");\n                }\n\n                // Retry the original command once with timeout.\n                let mut retry_cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n                retry_cmd\n                    .args(args)\n                    .current_dir(dir)\n                    .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n                    .kill_on_drop(true);\n                let retry_child = retry_cmd\n                    .spawn()\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br retry with args: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n                let retry =\n                    match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, retry_child.wait_with_output())\n                        .await\n                    {\n                        Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n                        Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                            return Err(e).context(format!(\"br retry failed: {args:?}\"));\n                        }\n                        Err(_) => {\n                            tracing::error!(\n                                args = ?args,\n                                timeout_secs,\n                                \"br retry timed out, killing process\"\n                            );\n                            bail!(\"br retry subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n                        }\n                    };\n\n                let retry_stdout = String::from_utf8(retry.stdout)\n                    .context(\"br retry stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n                let retry_stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&retry.stderr).into_owned();\n\n                if !retry.status.success() {\n                    let retry_code = retry.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n                    return Err(anyhow::Error::new(SyncRecoveryError {\n                        reason: format!(\n                            \"exit code {retry_code} after br sync retry\\n\\\n                             stderr: {retry_stderr}\\nstdout: {retry_stdout}\"\n                        ),\n                    }));\n                }\n\n                return Ok(retry_stdout);\n            }\n\n            bail!(\"br {args:?} exited with code {code}\\nstderr: {stderr}\\nstdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Run br and return both exit code and stdout (for claim race detection).\n    ///\n    /// Auto-recovers from SYNC_CONFLICT (exit code 6): runs `br sync` then\n    /// retries the original command once.\n    async fn run_br_with_status(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<(i32, String)> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS);\n\n        // kill_on_drop ensures the process is killed if the wait_with_output\n        // future is dropped (e.g., on timeout), preventing orphaned br processes.\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"br subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs = Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS,\n                    \"br subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\n                    \"br subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\",\n                    timeout_secs = Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS\n                );\n            }\n        };\n\n        let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"br stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        // Auto-recover from SYNC_CONFLICT: run `br sync` then retry once.\n        if code != 0 && is_sync_conflict(&stderr) {\n            tracing::warn!(\n                args = ?args,\n                \"br hit SYNC_CONFLICT (run_br_with_status), running br sync and retrying\"\n            );\n            let sync_timeout = std::time::Duration::from_secs(60);\n            let _ = tokio::time::timeout(\n                sync_timeout,\n                tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path)\n                    .args([\"sync\"])\n                    .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n                    .output(),\n            )\n            .await;\n\n            let retry = tokio::time::timeout(\n                timeout_duration,\n                tokio::process::Command::new(&self.br_path)\n                    .args(args)\n                    .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n                    .output(),\n            )\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| {\n                format!(\n                    \"br retry subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\",\n                    timeout_secs = Self::DEFAULT_BR_TIMEOUT_SECS\n                )\n            })?\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn br retry with args: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n            let retry_code = retry.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            let retry_stdout =\n                String::from_utf8(retry.stdout).context(\"br retry stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n            return Ok((retry_code, retry_stdout));\n        }\n\n        Ok((code, stdout))\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a JSON array or JSONL stream of beads from br output.\n    fn parse_beads(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        if json.trim().is_empty() {\n            return Ok(vec![]);\n        }\n        // Try JSON array first, then fall back to JSONL (one object per line)\n        if let Ok(beads) = serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(json) {\n            return Ok(beads);\n        }\n        json.lines()\n            .filter(|l| !l.trim().is_empty())\n            .map(|line| {\n                serde_json::from_str::<Bead>(line)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{line}\"))\n            })\n            .collect()\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array (first element).\n    fn parse_single_bead(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let beads = Self::parse_beads(json, context)?;\n        beads\n            .into_iter()\n            .next()\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"{context} returned empty array\"))\n    }\n\n    /// Run `bf claim` for atomic bead selection and claiming.\n    ///\n    /// async fn run_bf_claim(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(30);\n\n        // Try to find bf on PATH or at the default install location\n        let bf_path = which::which(\"bf\").or_else(|_| {\n            let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n            let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/bf\"));\n            if candidate.exists() {\n                Ok(candidate)\n            } else {\n                Err(anyhow!(\"bf not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/bf\"))\n            }\n        });\n\n        let bf_path = match bf_path {\n            Ok(p) => p,\n            Err(e) => {\n                return Err(e.context(\"bf CLI not found; falling back to br-style claim\"));\n            }\n        };\n\n        let args = [\"claim\", \"--assignee\", actor, \"--json\"];\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&bf_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(&self.workspace)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn bf subprocess: {:?}\", args))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"bf subprocess failed: {:?}\", args));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    \"bf subprocess timed out, killing code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            bail!(\n                \"bf {:?} exited with code {}\\nstderr: {}\",\n                args,\n                code,\n                stderr\n            );\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl BeadStore for BrCliBeadStore {\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let stdout = self\n fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let mut args = vec![\"ready\", \"--json\"];\n\n        // Build filter args — stored so they live long enough for the slice.\n        let assignee_arg;\n        if let Some(ref assignee) = filters.assignee {\n            args.push(\"--assignee\");\n            assignee_arg = assignee.clone();\n            args.push(&assignee_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_br(&args).await.context(\"br ready failed\")?;\n        let mut beads = Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"br ready --json\")?;\n\n        // Apply label exclusion async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        // Attempt claim by setting status=in_progress and assignee.\n        let (code, _stdout) = self\n            .run_br_with_status(&[\n                \"update\",\n                id_str,\n                \"--status\",\n                \"in_progress\",\n                \"--assignee\",\n                actor,\n            ])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"br update {id_str} (claim) failed to spawn\"))?;\n\n        match code {\n            0 => {\n                // Verify we actually won by reading back the bead.\n                let bead = self.show(id).await?;\n                if bead.assignee.as_deref() == Some(actor) {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n                } else {\n                    let claimed_by = bead\n                        .assignee\n                        .clone()\n                        .unwrap_or_else(|| \"(unknown)\".to_string());\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by })\n                }\n            }\n            4 => {\n                // br exit code 4 signals a conflict / optimistic lock failure.\n                let bead = self.show(id).await.ok();\n                let claimed_by = bead\n                    .and_then(|b| b.assignee)\n                    .unwrap_or_else(|| \"(unknown)\".to_string());\n                Ok(ClaimResult::RaceLost { claimed_by })\n            }\n            _ => Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: format!(\"br update exited with code {code}\"),\n            }),\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n  // Step 1: Remove the corrupt SQLite database.\n        if db_path.exists() {\n            tokio::fs::remove_file(&db_path)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove {}\", db_path.display()))?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %db_path.display(), \"removed corrupt database file\");\n        }\n\n        // Also remove WAL and SHM files if present.\n        for suffix in &[\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n            let wal_path = self.workspace.join(format!(\".beads/beads.db{suffix}\"));\n            if wal_path.exists() {\n                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(&wal_path).await;\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Reimport from JSONL.\n        self.run_br(&[\"sync\", \"--import-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br sync --import-only failed during full rebuild\")?;\n\n        // Step 3: Verify with br doctor.\n        let verify = self\n            .run_br(&[\"doctor\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"br doctor verification failed after rebuild\")?;\n        let report = Self::parse_doctor_output(&verify);\n\n        if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                report.warnings\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL — verified clean\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Use bf claim's atomic select-score-update to eliminate TOCTOU race.\n        // bf claim performs scoring (downstream_impact + critical_float + priority)\n        // and the UPDATE in a single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing\n        // that concurrent workers receive distinct beads.\n        match self.run_bf_claim(actor).await {\n            Ok(stdout) => {\n                // bf claim returns JSON with bead_id or empty object for no candidates\n                let trimmed = stdout.trim();\n                if trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed == \"{}\" || trimmed == \"null\" {\n                    return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    });\n                }\n\n                // Parse the JSON response from bf claim\n                #[derive(serde::Deserialize)]\n                struct BfClaimResponse {\n                    bead_id: Option<String>,\n                    #[allow(dead_code)]\n                    assignee: Option<String>,\n                }\n\n                let response: BfClaimResponse = serde_json::from_str(trimmed)\n                    .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {}\", trimmed))?;\n\n                if let Some(bead_id) = response.bead_id {\n                    // Fetch the full bead details\n                    self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id))\n                        .await\n                        .map(ClaimResult::Claimed)\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                // If bf is not available, fall back to the old br-style pattern\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"bf claim failed, falling back to br-style ready+claim\");\n                let filters = Filters::default();\n                let candidates = self.ready(&filters).await?;\n                if let Some(bead) = candidates.first() {\n                    self.claim(&bead.id, actor).await\n                } else {\n                    Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                        reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                    })\n                }\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nimpl BrCliBeadStore {\n    /// Parse `br doctor` output into a `RepairReport`.\n    fn parse_doctor_output(stdout: &str) -> RepairReport {\n        let mut report = RepairReport::default();\n        for line in stdout.lines() {\n            if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"WARN \") {\n                // Filter out non-actionable warnings that cannot be repaired\n                // (e.g., sqlite3 binary not installed on the system, or\n                // leftover recovery backup files from a prior repair/rebuild).\n                if rest.contains(\"sqlite3 not available\") || rest.contains(\"recovery_artifacts\") {\n                    continue;\n                }\n                report.warnings.push(rest.to_string());\n            } else if let Some(rest) = line.strip_prefix(\"FIXED \") {\n                report.fixed.push(rest.to_string());\n            }\n        }\n        report\n    }\n\n    /// Attempt database recovery: try repair first, then full rebuild.\n    ///\n    /// Returns the outcome of the recovery attempt. This is the primary\n    /// entry point for auto-recovery from SQLite corruption.\n    pub async fn recover_db(&self) -> RecoveryOutcome {\n        // Step 1: Try br doctor --repair.\n        tracing::warn!(\"attempting database recovery via br doctor --repair\");\n        match self.doctor_repair().await {\n            Ok(report) => {\n                tracing::info!(\n                    warnings = report.warnings.len(),\n                    fixed = report.fixed.len(),\n                    \"br doctor --repair completed\"\n                );\n                return RecoveryOutcome::Repaired(report);\n            }\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::warn!(error = %e, \"br doctor --repair failed, attempting full rebuild\");\n            }\n        }\n\n        // Step 2: Full rebuild — rm db + br sync --import + verify.\n        match self.full_rebuild().await {\n            Ok(()) => RecoveryOutcome::Rebuilt,\n            Err(e) => {\n                tracing::error!(error = %e, \"full database rebuild failed — JSONL may be corrupt\");\n                RecoveryOutcome::Failed(e)\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── BfCliBeadStore ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────\n\n/// `bf` CLI-backed bead store implementation.\n///\n/// Uses `bf claim` for atomic server-selected bead claiming. This eliminates\n/// the race condition in `BrCliBeadStore.claim()` where two workers could both\n/// see the same bead in `ready()` and race to claim it.\n///\n/// The key difference: `bf claim` atomically selects AND claims a bead in a\n/// single BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, guaranteeing that concurrent workers\n/// receive distinct beads.\npub struct BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Path to the `bf` binary.\n    pub bf_path: PathBuf,\n    /// Workspace root (directory containing `.beads/`).\n    pub workspace: PathBuf,\n    /// Model name for telemetry (e.g., \"claude-opus-4-7\").\n    pub model: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness name for telemetry (e.g., \"needle\").\n    pub harness: Option<String>,\n    /// Harness version for telemetry.\n    pub harness_version: Option<String>,\n}\n\nimpl BfCliBeadStore {\n    /// Construct a new store, validating that the `bf` binary exists.\n    pub fn new(\n        bf_path: PathBuf,\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        if !bf_path.exists() {\n            bail!(\"bf binary not found at {}\", bf_path.display());\n        }\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Try to find `bf` on PATH or the default install location.\n    pub fn discover(\n        workspace: PathBuf,\n        model: Option<String>,\n        harness: Option<String>,\n        harness_version: Option<String>,\n    ) -> Result<Self> {\n        let bf_path = which::which(\"bf\")\n            .or_else(|_| {\n                let home = std::env::var(\"HOME\").unwrap_or_default();\n                let candidate = PathBuf::from(format!(\"{home}/.local/bin/bf\"));\n                if candidate.exists() {\n                    Ok(candidate)\n                } else {\n                    Err(anyhow!(\"bf not found on PATH or at ~/.local/bin/bf\"))\n                }\n            })\n            .context(\"bf CLI not found; install bead-forge\")?;\n        Ok(BfCliBeadStore {\n            bf_path,\n            workspace,\n            model,\n            harness,\n            harness_version,\n        })\n    }\n\n    /// Default timeout for bf subprocess calls (30 seconds).\n    const DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS: u64 = 30;\n\n    /// Run a `bf` subcommand in the workspace directory and return stdout.\n    async fn run_bf(&self, args: &[&str]) -> Result<String> {\n        self.run_bf_in(&self.workspace, args, Self::DEFAULT_BF_TIMEOUT_SECS)\n            .await\n    }\n\n    async fn run_bf_in(&self, dir: &Path, args: &[&str], timeout_secs: u64) -> Result<String> {\n        let timeout_duration = std::time::Duration::from_secs(timeout_secs);\n\n        let mut cmd = tokio::process::Command::new(&self.bf_path);\n        cmd.args(args)\n            .current_dir(dir)\n            .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped())\n            .kill_on_drop(true);\n        let child = cmd\n            .spawn()\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to spawn bf subprocess: {args:?}\"))?;\n\n        let output = match tokio::time::timeout(timeout_duration, child.wait_with_output()).await {\n            Ok(Ok(output)) => output,\n            Ok(Err(e)) => {\n                return Err(e).context(format!(\"bf subprocess failed: {args:?}\"));\n            }\n            Err(_) => {\n                tracing::error!(\n                    args = ?args,\n                    timeout_secs,\n                    \"bf subprocess timed out, killing process\"\n                );\n                bail!(\"bf subprocess timed out after {timeout_secs}s: {args:?}\");\n            }\n        };\n\n        let stdout = String::from_utf8(output.stdout).context(\"bf stdout was not valid UTF-8\")?;\n        let stderr = String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr);\n\n        if !output.status.success() {\n            let code = output.status.code().unwrap_or(-1);\n            bail!(\"bf {args:?} exited with code {code}\\nstderr: {stderr}\\nstdout: {stdout}\");\n        }\n\n        Ok(stdout)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a JSON array of beads from bf output.\n    /// Handles both JSON array format `[{...},{...}]` and NDJSON (one object per line).\n    ///\n    /// A single unparseable NDJSON line (e.g. a bead carrying a status value\n    /// this build of NEEDLE doesn't yet recognize) is logged loudly and\n    /// skipped rather than failing the entire list — one bad record used to\n    /// take down `list_all()` for every workspace it appeared in, which broke\n    /// Weave/Mend/Unravel/Knot (all of which need the full bead list) on\n    /// every single cycle. This is NOT the same \"silently treat as empty\" v1\n    /// bug the module doc warns about: that bug swallowed failures and\n    /// returned nothing; this still surfaces every bad record via a loud\n    /// warning, it just doesn't discard the records that DID parse.\n    fn parse_beads(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let trimmed = json.trim();\n        if trimmed.is_empty() {\n            return Ok(vec![]);\n        }\n        // Try JSON array first (bf show returns [...])\n        if trimmed.starts_with('[') {\n            return serde_json::from_str::<Vec<Bead>>(trimmed)\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"JSON parse error from {context}:\\n{json}\"));\n        }\n        // Fall back to NDJSON (bf list returns one object per line)\n        let mut beads = Vec::new();\n        for line in trimmed.lines() {\n            let line = line.trim();\n            if line.is_empty() {\n                continue;\n            }\n            match serde_json::from_str::<Bead>(line) {\n                Ok(bead) => beads.push(bead),\n                Err(e) => {\n                    tracing::error!(\n                        context = %context,\n                        error = %e,\n                        line = %line,\n                        \"NDJSON parse error on one record — skipping this bead, \\\n                         keeping the rest of the list intact\"\n                    );\n                }\n            }\n        }\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    /// Parse a single bead from a JSON array (first element).\n    fn parse_single_bead(json: &str, context: &str) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let beads = Self::parse_beads(json, context)?;\n        beads\n            .into_iter()\n            .next()\n            .ok_or_else(|| anyhow!(\"{context} returned empty array\"))\n    }\n}\n\n#[async_trait]\nimpl BeadStore for BfCliBeadStore {\n    async fn list_all(&self) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"list\", \"--json\", \"--limit\", \"0\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf list --json failed\")?;\n        Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")\n    }\n\n    async fn ready(&self, filters: &Filters) -> Result<Vec<Bead>> {\n        let mut args = vec![\"list\", \"--json\", \"--status\", \"open\", \"--limit\", \"0\"];\n\n        // Build filter args — stored so they live long enough for the slice.\n        let assignee_arg;\n        if let Some(ref assignee) = filters.assignee {\n            args.push(\"--assignee\");\n            assignee_arg = assignee.clone();\n            args.push(&assignee_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf list failed\")?;\n        let mut beads = Self::parse_beads(&stdout, \"bf list --json\")?;\n\n        // Apply label exclusion filter (bf CLI doesn't support this natively).\n        if !filters.exclude_labels.is_empty() {\n            beads.retain(|b| !b.labels.iter().any(|l| filters.exclude_labels.contains(l)));\n        }\n\n        Ok(beads)\n    }\n\n    async fn show(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Bead> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"show\", id_str, \"--json\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf show {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Self::parse_single_bead(&stdout, &format!(\"bf show {id_str} --json\"))\n    }\n\n    async fn claim(&self, _id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // BfCliBeadStore uses atomic claim_auto() for all claim operations.\n        // This eliminates the race condition from the old br-style\n        // \"update + show verify\" pattern — two workers racing to claim\n        // the same bead will always receive distinct beads.\n        self.claim_auto(actor).await\n    }\n\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult> {\n        // Build bf claim args\n        let mut args = vec![\"claim\", \"--assignee\", actor, \"--json\"];\n\n        // Optional telemetry args\n        let model_arg;\n        let harness_arg;\n        let harness_version_arg;\n\n        if let Some(ref model) = self.model {\n            args.push(\"--model\");\n            model_arg = model.as_str();\n            args.push(model_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness) = self.harness {\n            args.push(\"--harness\");\n            harness_arg = harness.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_arg);\n        }\n        if let Some(ref harness_version) = self.harness_version {\n            args.push(\"--harness-version\");\n            harness_version_arg = harness_version.as_str();\n            args.push(harness_version_arg);\n        }\n\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&args).await.context(\"bf claim failed\")?;\n\n        // Parse JSON output: {\"bead_id\": \"...\", \"reclaimed\": 0, \"assignee\": \"...\"}\n        let json: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&stdout)\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf claim returned invalid JSON: {stdout}\"))?;\n\n        if let Some(bead_id) = json.get(\"bead_id\").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {\n            if bead_id.is_empty() || stdout.contains(\"No beads available\") {\n                return Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                    reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n                });\n            }\n            // Fetch the full bead details\n            let bead = self.show(&BeadId::from(bead_id)).await?;\n            Ok(ClaimResult::Claimed(bead))\n        } else {\n            Ok(ClaimResult::NotClaimable {\n                reason: \"no beads available\".to_string(),\n            })\n        }\n    }\n\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"update\", id_str, \"--status\", \"open\", \"--assignee\", \"\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf release {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        self.run_bf(&[\"sync\", \"--flush-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf sync --flush-only failed\")?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"reopen\", id_str])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf reopen {id_str} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>> {\n        let bead = self.show(id).await?;\n        Ok(bead.labels)\n    }\n\n    async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"label\", \"add\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf label add {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()> {\n        let id_str = id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"label\", \"remove\", id_str, \"--label\", label])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf label remove {id_str} {label} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str, labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId> {\n        let mut args: Vec<String> = vec![\n            \"create\".into(),\n            \"--title\".into(),\n            title.into(),\n            \"--description\".into(),\n            body.into(),\n        ];\n        for label in labels {\n            args.push(\"--label\".into());\n            args.push((*label).into());\n        }\n        let arg_refs: Vec<&str> = args.iter().map(|s| s.as_str()).collect();\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&arg_refs).await.context(\"bf create failed\")?;\n        let id_str = stdout.trim();\n        if id_str.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\"bf create returned empty ID\");\n        }\n        Ok(BeadId::from(id_str))\n    }\n\n    async fn add_dependency(&self, blocker_id: &BeadId, blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"dep\", \"add\", blocked, blocker, \"--type\", \"blocks\"])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep add {blocked} {blocker} --type blocks failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()> {\n        let blocked = blocked_id.as_ref();\n        let blocker = blocker_id.as_ref();\n        self.run_bf(&[\"dep\", \"remove\", blocked, blocker])\n            .await\n            .with_context(|| format!(\"bf dep remove {blocked} {blocker} failed\"))?;\n        Ok(())\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"doctor\", \"--repair\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf doctor --repair failed\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport> {\n        let stdout = self.run_bf(&[\"doctor\"]).await.context(\"bf doctor failed\")?;\n        Ok(BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&stdout))\n    }\n\n    async fn full_rebuild(&self) -> Result<()> {\n        let db_path = self.workspace.join(\".beads/beads.db\");\n\n        if db_path.exists() {\n            tokio::fs::remove_file(&db_path)\n                .await\n                .with_context(|| format!(\"failed to remove {}\", db_path.display()))?;\n            tracing::info!(path = %db_path.display(), \"removed corrupt database file\");\n        }\n\n        for suffix in &[\"-wal\", \"-shm\"] {\n            let wal_path = self.workspace.join(format!(\".beads/beads.db{suffix}\"));\n            if wal_path.exists() {\n                let _ = tokio::fs::remove_file(&wal_path).await;\n            }\n        }\n\n        self.run_bf(&[\"sync\", \"--import-only\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf sync --import-only failed during full rebuild\")?;\n\n        let verify = self\n            .run_bf(&[\"doctor\"])\n            .await\n            .context(\"bf doctor verification failed after rebuild\")?;\n        let report = BrCliBeadStore::parse_doctor_output(&verify);\n\n        if !report.warnings.is_empty() {\n            bail!(\n                \"database still has issues after rebuild: {:?}\",\n                report.warnings\n            );\n        }\n\n        tracing::info!(\"database fully rebuilt from JSONL — verified clean\");\n        Ok(())\n    }\n}\n\n// ─── Unit tests `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `RaceLost { claimed_by }` — another worker got there first.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — bead not in a claimable state.\n    async fn claim(&self, id: &BeadId, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Atomically find and claim the next available bead (server-selected).\n    ///\n    /// This is the preferred method for multi-worker scenarios as it eliminates\n    /// race conditions: the server selects the bead and assigns it in a single\n    /// BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. Two workers calling this simultaneously will\n    /// always receive distinct beads.\n    ///\n    /// Returns a `ClaimResult` describing the outcome:\n    /// - `Claimed(bead)` — success, returns the full bead.\n    /// - `NotClaimable { reason }` — no beads available to claim.\n    async fn claim_auto(&self, actor: &str) -> Result<ClaimResult>;\n\n    /// Release a claimed bead back to open (e.g., after agent failure).\n    async fn release(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Flush local bead changes to JSONL before release.\n    ///\n    /// Runs `br sync --flush-only` to ensure any local writes are persisted\n    /// to JSONL before attempting to release a bead. This prevents SYNC_CONFLICT\n    /// errors when the JSONL has newer remote changes.\n    async fn flush(&self) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Reopen a closed (Done) bead back to open status.\n    ///\n    /// Used by validation gates when verification fails after an agent has\n    /// already closed the bead.\n    async fn reopen(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// List all labels on a bead.\n    async fn labels(&self, id: &BeadId) -> Result<Vec<String>>;\n\n    /// Add a label to a bead.\n    async fn add_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Remove a label from a bead.\n    async fn remove_label(&self, id: &BeadId, label: &str) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Create a new bead and return its ID.\n    async fn create_bead(&self, title: &str, body: &str, labels: &[&str]) -> Result<BeadId>;\n\n    /// Add a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep add <blocker_id> --blocks <blocked_id>`.\n    async fn add_dependency(&self, blocker_id: &BeadId, blocked_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Remove a dependency link: `blocker_id` blocks `blocked_id`.\n    ///\n    /// Uses `br dep remove <blocked_id> <blocker_id>`.\n    async fn remove_dependency(&self, blocked_id: &BeadId, blocker_id: &BeadId) -> Result<()>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor --repair` and return the report.\n    async fn doctor_repair(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Run `br doctor` (without `--repair`) to check database health.\n    ///\n    /// Returns warnings if any issues are detected, without attempting to fix them.\n    async fn doctor_check(&self) -> Result<RepairReport>;\n\n    /// Full database rebuild: remove SQLite DB and reimport from JSONL.\n    ///\n    /// 1. rm .beads/beads.db\n    /// 2. br sync --import\n    /// 3.
